sentence: By practicing this kind of detachment, you can free yourself from the bondage of worrying about whether your actions lead to good or bad results [9.28].

sentence: Ultimately, letting go of the fruits of your work is a way to find peace of mind [12.12].

sentence: For those who remain attached to this vision, there is a sense of being cared for and supported in what they possess [9.22].

sentence: It is suggested that you engage in your tasks without personal expectations, ego, or the fever of anxiety [3.30].

sentence: If that feels difficult, you can simply try to act while renouncing the results of your work and keeping your mind steady [12.11].

sentence: By depending on the Divine and working under that protection, you can remain conscious of that connection in all your activities [18.57].

sentence: It is suggested that you can look at your own mind as either your friend or your enemy, and it is up to you to lift yourself up [6.5].

sentence: If you find it difficult to follow specific spiritual practices, you might simply dedicate your daily work to the Divine, as this can also lead to a sense of perfection [12.10].

sentence: Working in a spirit of devotion is described as being a very effective path [5.2].

sentence: It is noted that performing actions just to gain honor, respect, or worship from others is considered unstable and temporary [17.18].
verse_text: That austerity which is undertaken for earning a name, being honoured and worshipped, and also ostentatiously,-that is spoken of as born of rajas, belonging to this world, uncertain and transitory.

sentence: If you are looking for peace of mind, the Gita suggests that letting go of the desire for the results of your actions is even more helpful than meditation or knowledge [12.12].

sentence: It is suggested that those who fix their minds on the personal form of the Divine with great faith are considered the most perfect yogis [12.2].

sentence: You might find that by keeping your mind focused on the Divine with faith, you become the most intimately united and the best among all those who practice yoga [6.47].

sentence: If you choose to worship with faith, the Divine supports and strengthens that very commitment within you [7.21].

sentence: It is quite common to feel bewildered when trying to determine the best path forward, as even the intelligent can find themselves confused about what constitutes the right action [4.16].

sentence: You might feel as though you are receiving conflicting signals, leading you to wonder which choice will truly be the most beneficial [3.2].

sentence: The Gita suggests that knowledge, actions, and the people performing them are categorized into three types based on the different modes of nature [18.19].

sentence: It is helpful to remember that different approaches can lead to the same result, and those who see these paths as fundamentally the same are seeing things as they truly are [5.5].

sentence: By applying yourself well to one path, you can achieve the same outcome that others reach through different methods [5.4].

sentence: Knowing yourself involves recognizing that the soul is invisible, inconceivable, and unchanging, which helps one move past grief for the body [2.25].

sentence: You might find it helpful to approach those who have realized the truth, asking them questions and serving them so they can share their knowledge with you [4.34].

sentence: True knowledge is described as being steadfast in understanding the self and contemplating the ultimate goal of reality [13.12].

sentence: It is also suggested that everything else, which is not this self-knowledge, is considered ignorance [13.12].
verse_text: Steadfastness in the knowledge of the Self, contemplation on the Goal of the knowledge of Reality-this is spoken of as Knowledge. Ignorance is that which is other than this.

sentence: You can also look at how material nature and the individual soul are both beginningless, with all changes and qualities arising from nature itself [13.20].

sentence: By becoming fixed in this kind of knowledge, one can attain a transcendental nature that remains undisturbed by the cycles of creation and dissolution [14.2].
verse_text: Those who attain identity with Me by resorting of this Knowledge are not born even during creation, nor do they suffer pain during dissolution.

sentence: It is interesting to consider that even those who are considered intelligent can sometimes be confused about what constitutes the right course of action [4.16].

sentence: This happens because people can become deeply attached to the activities driven by the modes of nature, which can cloud their judgment [3.29].
verse_text: Those who are wholly deluded by the gunas of Nature become attached to the activities of the gunas. The knower of the All should not disturb those of dull intellect, who do not know the All.

sentence: While intelligence is a powerful tool, it is helpful to remember that the senses and the mind also play a significant role in how we perceive the world [3.42].
verse_text: They say that the organs are superior (to the gross body); the mind is superior to the organs; but the intellect is superior to the mind. However, the one who is superior to the intellect is He.

sentence: Sometimes, a person may be so caught up in these material influences that they fail to see the deeper reality of their situation [15.10].

sentence: A sober person, however, remains steady and is not easily bewildered by the constant changes that occur in life [2.13].
